name: Radio Broadcast Hub
tag: Drafts broadcast bulletins and runs practice on-air segments with AI voices, so your desk is ready before it matters.

scenarios.title: Severe weather bulletin
scenarios.ask: A high wind warning covers {counties} counties in our listening area. Draft the bulletin, voice it in {languages}, and repeat it every {interval}.
steps: Intake
Read the sample weather alert: winds up to 60 mph, outages likely, {counties} counties named.
Writer
Drafted a {=30 + counties * 4}-second bulletin: headline, areas, what to do, source and next update time.
Translator
Produced {=languages} language versions and kept the county names and times identical in each.
Voice studio
Rendered each version with a calm AI news voice. You can play every take before it airs.
Scheduler
Built a 3-hour repeat plan: {=floor(180 / interval)} airings per language, placed between songs and ad breaks.
followups: Is this an official Emergency Alert System message?
No. The hub drafts and voices bulletins for your own programming. Official EAS activations still run through your station's EAS equipment and procedures.
What if the warning gets updated?
Paste or import the new alert and the Writer marks what changed. The new versions replace the old ones in the repeat plan once you approve them.
Can a person read it instead?
Yes. The script prints with timing marks, so a host can read it live and the AI voice stays as a backup.

scenarios.title: Daily commercial log
scenarios.ask: Build tomorrow's log for {stations} stations: {spots} ad spots an hour across {hours} hours of programming.
steps: Traffic agent
Placed {=spots * hours * stations} spots across {stations} stations and checked each against its contract run dates.
Separation check
Kept competing advertisers apart. Moved {=max(1, round(spots * hours * stations * 0.02))} spots that landed in the same break as a competitor.
Copy desk
Matched every spot to its current audio file. {=max(1, round(stations * 1.5))} spots point to expired copy and were flagged.
Voice studio
Recorded fresh station IDs and liners with the house AI voice for each hour.
followups: Can it export to our playout system?
Yes. The log exports as a standard text or CSV file that most playout and traffic systems can import. Sample data here, of course.
What happens to the flagged spots?
They stay in the log with a warning until sales sends new copy. If nothing arrives, the agent suggests a filler spot of the same length.

scenarios.title: Practice a live broadcast
scenarios.ask: Run a {length} practice show with {hosts} AI co-hosts and {calls} simulated listener calls so our new producer can train.
steps: Show planner
Built a run-down with {=max(2, round(length / 10))} segments, a news break and a traffic slot.
Script writer
Wrote banter and transitions for {hosts} co-host voices, about {=round(length * 0.6)} minutes of talk.
Caller simulator
Prepared {calls} listener calls, including one with a bad line and one that runs long.
Coach
Logs every late cue and dead-air gap so the producer can review the run afterward.
followups: Does this go out over the air?
No. Practice shows run inside the hub only. Nothing reaches your transmitter or stream unless you send it there on purpose.
How does the coach score the run?
It counts missed cues and gaps over 3 seconds and lists them with timestamps. It's a training aid, not a formal grade.
